facts.statement: Silvisaurus is a nodosaurid ankylosaur whose name combines Latin for woodland and Greek for lizard.
facts.quote: Silvisaurus, from the Latin silva "woodland" and Greek sauros "lizard", is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Early to Late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The species was discovered in the 1950s by Kansas rancher Warren W. Condray.
facts.quote: A fossil of the species was discovered in the 1950s by rancher Warren W. Condray of Wells, Kansas.

facts.statement: The dinosaur skeleton was recovered in July 1955 with the help of the discoverer.
facts.quote: In July 1955 Camp, with help from Condray, recovered the skeleton of a dinosaur.

facts.statement: The species was formally described and named by Theodore H. Eaton Jr. in 1960.
facts.quote: In 1960 the find was described and named by Theodore H. Eaton Jr., also from the University of Kansas, as the type species Silvisaurus condrayi.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the animal's likely habitat in a densely forested area.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin silva, "wood", in reference to the probably densely forested habitat of the animal.

facts.statement: The species name honors the rancher who discovered the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Condray.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Terra Cotta Clay Member of the Dakota Formation in Kansas.
facts.quote: The holotype, KU 10296, was found in exposures of the Terra Cotta Clay Member of the Dakota Formation (late Albian-early Cenomanian) in Kansas

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an incomplete skeleton including the skull, neck, back, tail, and leg bones.
facts.quote: It includes the mandible, eight neck vertebrae, ten dorsal vertebrae, a sacrum of six sacral vertebrae, three tail vertebrae, a left pubis fragment, the lower end of the right femur, and a toe phalanx.

facts.statement: Disarticulated armor plates and spikes were found alongside the main skeleton.
facts.quote: Additionally disarticulated plates and spikes from the body armour were discovered.

facts.statement: The fossil condition was poor due to exposure in a dry riverbed and damage from cattle.
facts.quote: The condition of the fossil was poor as the bones had been exposed at the bottom of a dry riverbed and had been weathered and trampled by cattle.

facts.statement: The skull measures 33 cm in length and 25 cm in width.
facts.quote: Its skull measures 33 cm in length and is 25 cm wide.

facts.statement: The lower jaw contains at least twenty-five teeth.
facts.quote: The dentary includes at least twenty-five teeth

facts.statement: Each upper jaw bone holds between eight and nine teeth.
facts.quote: each premaxilla holds eight to nine teeth.

facts.statement: Teeth at the front of the jaw suggest Silvisaurus was a relatively primitive nodosaurid compared to later forms with beaks.
facts.quote: The presence of teeth at the front of the jaw suggests that this may have been a relatively primitive nodosaur, since most later forms had a toothless beak instead.

facts.statement: Silvisaurus likely possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail in addition to standard armor plates.
facts.quote: In addition to the usual rounded and polygonal osteoderms, Silvisaurus may have also sported bony spines on its shoulders and tail.

facts.statement: Large air passages in the head suggest the animal may have produced loud vocalizations for communication.
facts.quote: The head contained large air passages, which may have been used for loud vocalisations, presumably for communication.

facts.statement: Silvisaurus is classified as a relatively primitive nodosaurid.
facts.quote: This taxon represents a relatively primitive nodosaurid

facts.statement: Research indicates Silvisaurus forms a basal group with Sauropelta and Pawpawsaurus, nested deep within the nodosaurid family tree.
facts.quote: Vickaryous et al. (2004) have stated that "Sauropelta edwardsorum, Silvisaurus condrayi, and Pawpawsaurus campbelli form a basal polytomy nested deep to Cedarpelta."

facts.statement: Silvisaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 105 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 113 y 105 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Silvisaurus is estimated from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Silvisaurus possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail.
facts.quote: Silvisaurus may have also sported bony spines on its shoulders and tail.

rejected.statement: Silvisaurus is the only dinosaur species named from terrestrial deposits in Kansas and was designated the official state land fossil in 2023.
rejected.quote: It is the only known dinosaur species named from terrestrial deposits in Kansas and was designated the official state land fossil in 2023.

rejected.statement: The animal is estimated to have been approximately 4 meters long.
rejected.quote: Based on the remains, the animal is estimated to have been approximately 4 m in length.
